title: Potunk Neck (Westhampton)
summary: Potunk is a Westhampton placename for Potunk Neck and nearby meadowland, recorded in seventeenth-century Southampton and East Hampton references and interpreted as a boggy place.
map_geometry_source: Approximate Westhampton point for Potunk Neck, placed between nearby Apocock/Beaverdam Creek, Monabaugs, and Ketchaponack records; exact neck, point, and meadow boundaries need local map review.
introduction_content: Potunk is associated with a Westhampton locality and neck landscape west of Ketchaponack and near Monabaugs in western Southampton town.
history_content: Potunk belongs to the Westhampton neck-and-meadow landscape alongside Apocock, Monabaugs, Ketchaponack, and Wonunke. Boundary and meadow details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
Related forms include Potuncke, Potunck, Potunk, and Potonke. The name is interpreted as a bog, a place where the foot sinks, or land where one sinks in mire.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are among the most interesting and powerful documents we have for exploring changes to landscape over time.”

— William Cronon, Names on the Land: Place Names as Historical Evidence (2018), Section I, Why study place names?

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point in the Westhampton Potunk Neck vicinity. This marker is not an exact seventeenth-century neck, point, meadow, or boundary coordinate.
